newsitem.title: UK: UK's telecom co Ionica to make market debut.
newsitem.headline: UK's telecom co Ionica to make market debut.

text.p: Ionica Plc, a new entrant in Britain's almost monopolistic telecommunications market, will make its debut on London's stock exchange and America's Nasdaq stock markets next week, at a valuation of about 640 million pounds ($1.1 billion).
The Cambridge-based wireless telephony operator announced on Friday that it had offered 40 million shares priced at 390 pence each to raise about 147 million pounds.

Ionica's chief executive Nigel Playford said the issue proceeds, combined with a credit facility of 300 million pounds, offered financial stability for it to plan for the future, much of which would involve attracting customers away from behemoth British Telecommunications plc.
Ionica uses radio links to deliver telephone signals and has more than 21,000 customers in the eastern and midlands regions of the UK.
Dealings in the company's shares are expected to commence on a conditional basis at 1330 GMT on July 25.

The company said the holders of outstanding warrants had exercised warrants -- conditional on closing of the offering expected on July 25 -- over 8.4 million ordinary shares at an exercise price of 275 pence per share.
The exercise of warrants will raise additional proceeds to Ionica of about 23.2 million pounds.
The ordinary shares sold in the offering represent 24 percent of the enlarged issued ordinary share capital of Ionica.
The existing shareholders have agreed not to sell their holdings for the next 12 months.
Riding on the technology truth that air is cheaper than cable and wires, Ionica is offering its customers calls at a 15 percent discount to BT, a research report by Lehman Brothers said.
Ionica uses fixed Radio access (FRA) technology which employs a cellular-like network of base stations to provide the link to a radio receiver installed on the roof of chimney to a subscriber's home.

"The FRA technology significantly reduces its economies of scale disadvantage," Lehman said adding that Ionica which currently has a 2 1/2 percent of UK's residential market could achieve 10 percent in the long term. ($ = 0.598 British Pounds)
